title: University Students Involved in Voyeurism and Sexual Harassment Cases
what_it_is: University Students Involved in Voyeurism and Sexual Harassment Cases

sections.label: Questions on student sexual misconduct
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Education about reported sexual harassment, misconduct and serious disciplinary cases at autonomous universities and institutes of higher learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education in the past three years (a) how many cases of sexual harassment or misconduct have been reported by undergraduate students in each of the autonomous universities; and (b) how many of such cases have been referred to the Police for prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many cases of serious disciplinary cases involving students at our institutes of higher learning (IHLs) have there been over the last three years; (b) how many students have been expelled; and (c) how does the Ministry ensure that the disciplinary frameworks for the IHLs are robust and consistent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) for each year from 2008, how many cases of on campus sexual harassment and sexual assault at autonomous universities were reported to the campus authorities; (b) how many resulted in administrative penalties from campus authorities and no further action; (c) how many resulted in administrative penalties and Police action; (d) what was the nature of the administrative punishments issued; (e) what were the considerations behind determining administrative penalties; and (f) what support was provided to victims in such cases.

sections.label: Sexual misconduct disciplinary cases
sections.summary: Over the past three years, the six AUs handled 42 disciplinary cases involving sexual misconduct within campuses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Over the past three years, the six AUs handled a total of 42 disciplinary cases involving sexual misconduct within campuses.

sections.label: 56 cases across six AUs
sections.summary: The reply covers all 56 cases, with 17 in Academic Year 2015, 18 in 2016 and 21 in 2017 across all six AUs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But since the focus of my reply today is on the penalty framework of the AUs rather than campus security, I will refer to all 56 cases today in my reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There were 17 cases in Academic Year 2015, 18 cases in Academic Year 2016, and 21 cases in Academic Year 2017 across all six AUs.

sections.label: Jail terms in 10 cases
sections.summary: Out of the remaining 31, 10 cases resulted in jail terms of between 10 days and eight months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Out of the remaining 31, 10 cases resulted in jail terms of between 10 days and eight months.

sections.label: Review of disciplinary frameworks
sections.summary: The Minister asked all AUs, polytechnics and the Institute of Technical Education to review their disciplinary frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As our circumstances change, the AUs must likewise keep up with the times and ensure that their policies and processes remain relevant in establishing a safe and supportive environment for all students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I have, therefore, asked all our AUs, polytechnics and the Institute of Technical Education to review their disciplinary frameworks.

sections.label: Committee preliminary recommendations timeline
sections.summary: Committee members will release preliminary recommendations in mid-May for consultations and aim to complete their work in June this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Committee members will release some preliminary recommendations in the middle of May for consultations and aim to complete their work in June this year.

sections.label: Campus safety and victim support
sections.summary: Monica Baey said her aim was fairness for perpetrator and victim in future cases, so AUs should improve campus safety and victim support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Ms Monica Baey herself has said that, as hurt and affected as she is, her objective in publicising her story was not to seek revenge for the present case, but to ensure fairness for both the perpetrator and the victim in future cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, the most important priority now is for the AUs to see how they can do better and take concrete steps to improve campus safety and their victim support frameworks and processes.
